page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the ARM64 AWS Graviton processor family, utilizing Neoverse-V2 physical cores. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with no hyperthreading, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance does not include local storage or discrete GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached EBS storage.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the top tier for multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and high-throughput operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing all register top-tier results. Additionally, memory bandwidth tests show exceptional read and write speeds, with uncached large-block reads reaching 480.96 GB/sec. Single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, remains in the average tier.

Network capabilities are a major highlight, featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps. This high-speed networking, combined with top-tier Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, makes the instance highly efficient for distributed workloads. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the high resource density of the ARMv9 architecture, offering strong multi-core performance per resource unit compared to traditional x86 alternatives, though workloads requiring x86-specific instruction sets will face compatibility tradeoffs.

This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive and network-bound workloads. Optimal use cases include large-scale software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, Redis caching layers, and medium-parameter LLM text generation.
